newsitem.title: DENMARK: Quiet Danish shares rise marginally, Novo in focus.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Danish shares rise marginally, Novo in focus.

text.p: Danish share prices closed a little higher on Tuesday, with dealers seeing little change until Wednesday noon when key blue chip Novo Nordisk's 1996 first nine-month result is expected.
"The market is quiet, prices steady up to the Novo result, which will determine the way things go," one dealer said.
A Reuter poll on Monday showed analysts expected Novo Nordisk to post 12 percent higher pre-tax profits for the year's first three quarters.
The KFX top-20 index finished 0.16 point up at 127.51 in overall bourse turnover of 485 million crowns.
The KFX December future rose 0.70 point to 128.25 with 1,067 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
In a relaxed market, the Novo share was in the limelight, rising over the 1,000 crown level at one point, only to slip back and close unchanged at 995 crowns.
Carlsberg brewery finished four crowns higher at 373 on increased earnings for its U.K.-based Carlsberg-Tetley joint venture, which released its 1995/96 result early in the day.
